conventions.convention: Finite metric graphs allow parallel edges and loops, have positive finite edge lengths and no isolated vertices, and count the two endpoint incidences of a loop separately. V_D imposes common vertex traces and zero anchor traces, but no derivative condition.
Edge coordinates run from tail to head; outward endpoint derivatives are -u′(0) at the tail and +u′(ℓ) at the head.

Finite weighted networks are simple graphs with incidence columns -1 at the tail and +1 at the head, nonnegative conductances, positive free-vertex masses, and principal Dirichlet restriction L_D of BCBᵀ. Zero conductances remove coupling.
Routing acts on incoming mass-flux columns through a nonnegative matrix whose incoming columns each sum to one; equal incident densities are not imposed.
The closed Neumann gauge K⊥ uses the standard Euclidean inner product and removes every positive-conductance component's constant mode; compatibility is b ∈ K⊥.
P1 meshes require a nonempty edge set and finitely many positive-length cells per edge; h is the maximum cell length. The energy rate assumes edgewise H² regularity explicitly.
Forward Euler positivity is an iff for the full step matrix, with the minimum over no positive diagonal stiffness entries interpreted as +∞.
Metric-graph endpoint representatives assume AC; the elliptic, parabolic and Galerkin interfaces explicitly also assume Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and that every connected edge component has an anchor in D. With L_Γ = Σ_e ℓ_e, every w ∈ V_D satisfies ‖w‖L²(Γ) ≤ L_Γ(Σ_e ‖w′_e‖L²(e)²)^(1/2).

For the weighted network data and zero extension x̄, xᵀL_Dx = Σ_e c_e(x̄_head(e) − x̄_tail(e))² ≥ 0. Its kernel consists exactly of positive-conductance componentwise constants that vanish on components meeting D. In the closed case, every differentiable solution satisfies d(1ᵀMu)/dt = 1ᵀf.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite metric graph and anchor set D, the trace-matching space and the anchored space V_D are closed real Hilbert subspaces of the edge-product H¹ space with its edge-product H¹ inner product.

Assume AC, edgewise u_e ∈ H², v ∈ V_D and constant κ_e > 0. Then Σ_e κ_e∫u′_ev′_e = −Σ_e κ_e∫u″_ev_e + Σ_z v(z)Σ_{ι∈I(z)}κ_e(ι)∂ν_ιu_e(ι)(z). Anchor test traces and free-vertex Kirchhoff sums remove their respective boundary terms.

Assume AC, any anchor set D, a conforming edge mesh, positive edge constants κ_e and edgewise H² u satisfying the V_D trace and anchor conditions. Its nodal interpolant belongs to V_h and satisfies (Σ_e κ_e‖(u_e−I_hu_e)′‖L²(e)²)^(1/2) ≤ h(Σ_e κ_e‖u″_e‖L²(e)²)^(1/2).

Assume AC and Countable Choice, a nonempty edge set, an anchor in every connected edge component and constant diffusivities bounded above and below by positive constants. Every f in the edge-product real L² space has a unique u ∈ V_D satisfying a(u,v) = Σ_e∫f_ev_e for all v ∈ V_D; under edgewise H² regularity its interior equation and natural free-vertex condition are the stated diffusion equation and Kirchhoff balance.
